capabilities: Manage files from a pane with named focus-zone shortcuts and cross-vault copy/paste
Batch rename, batch create, and batch edit YAML frontmatter with previews and presets
Manually sort files and folders with pinning, drag reorder, and per-folder sorting
Bulk rename, merge, delete, lock, and search tags; batch edit property types and values
Move files by tag or YAML conditions and hide or exclude files from the pane
disambiguation: Not a focus or distraction-free writing tool; "focus zones" are shortcut panes that hold links to the files and folders you are working on.
extras: Mobile support is experimental (no cross-vault or touch drag-and-drop); install is manual or via BRAT; uses some undocumented Obsidian internals that may break between versions; batch operations write directly to notes, so the README advises backing up first.
problem: Obsidian's built-in file explorer lacks shortcut zones for current work, cross-vault clipboard, batch rename/create, manual ordering, and bulk tag or property cleanup.

relations.evidence: Obsidian bookmarks sync: add or remove bookmarks from the menu and see bookmarked items marked.
plus Base, Canvas, Excalidraw (if the plugin is enabled) and your own custom file types

summary: File manager panel with focus-zone shortcuts, cross-vault copy/paste, batch renaming, manual sorting, plus tag and property managers.
